title: Underactuated Robotics: Highly-articulated Legged Robots
author: Russ Tedrake, MIT
snippet: Centroidal force/momentum balance, unilateral friction contacts, scope of ZMP and reduced models.
sections: Robots with massless legs; ZMP; Centroidal dynamics
claims: Net wrench balance constrains support; full joint feasibility needs additional constraints

title: Leveraging Cone Double Description for Multi-contact Stability of Humanoids with Applications to Statics and Dynamics
author: Stephane Caron, Quang-Cuong Pham, Yoshihiko Nakamura
snippet: Surface contact wrench cones include force and moment feasibility under friction and nonnegative normal load.
claims: Support polygon alone omits friction and other wrench constraints
Centroidal feasibility is conditional on kinematic compatibility and actuator assumptions

title: Optimization for Control and Planning of Multi-contact Dynamic Motion
author: Michael Posa, MIT
snippet: Contact complementarity forbids force across a positive gap; contact and motion are jointly optimized.
claims: Contact order can be optimized rather than prescribed
Relaxed intermediate forces must not be accepted as final physical support

title: Discovery of Complex Behaviors through Contact-Invariant Optimization
author: Igor Mordatch, Emanuel Todorov, Zoran Popovic
snippet: Joint contact/trajectory optimization across activities; predefined patches, simplified inertia and no-slip limitations remain.
claims: Action-specific contact sequences are not necessary
Generic formulation does not mean prior-free or guaranteed global optimum

title: DECO: Dense Estimation of 3D Human-Scene Contact In The Wild
author: Shashank Tripathi et al.
snippet: Image body/scene context predicts binary surface contacts, not forces; imperfect geometric reconstructions can corrupt distance-based contact.
claims: Contact and body support are distinct
Visual context can propose contacts without a named action

title: HuMoR: 3D Human Motion Model for Robust Pose Estimation
author: Davis Rempe et al.
snippet: Temporal motion prior estimates motion, ground and contacts; full paper reports rare lying and static sitting failures.
claims: Temporal priors aid contact inference but cannot resolve all static/occluded cases

title: Differentiable Dynamics for Articulated 3D Human Motion Reconstruction
author: Erik Gartner, Mykhaylo Andriluka, Erwin Coumans, Cristian Sminchisescu
snippet: DiffPhy combines articulated physics, full-body contact and image losses; residual forces can improve pose metrics without physical explanation.
claims: Pose error is not a sufficient physical-support test
Full-body scene-contact reconstruction is a researched formulation

title: Trajectory Optimization for Physics-Based Reconstruction of 3D Human Pose From Monocular Video
author: Erik Gartner, Mykhaylo Andriluka, Hongyi Xu, Cristian Sminchisescu
snippet: Feature-complete simulated motion fitted to visual observations with full-body/scene interaction; distinct from DiffPhy.
claims: Scene geometry and physical body fitting are part of reconstruction, not supplied by a skeleton alone

title: World-Grounded Human Motion Recovery via Gravity-View Coordinates
author: Zehong Shen et al.
snippet: Predicts world motion and stationary probabilities for hands, toes and heels; these are not load-bearing forces.
claims: Existing upstream stationary evidence can be used as a prior, not support truth

title: Contact-guided Real2Sim from Monocular Video with Planar Scene Primitives
author: Zihan Wang et al.
snippet: CRISP fuses video contact, temporal filtering and scene geometry; near-contact errors, drift and rigid-scene assumptions limit inference.
claims: Video contacts need temporal and scene consistency
Incorrect body geometry can contaminate inferred support geometry

title: UniCon3R: Contact-aware 3D Human-Scene Reconstruction from Monocular Video
author: Tanuj Sur et al.
snippet: Preprint fuses video/scene/previous-contact evidence and feeds contact back into reconstruction; binary contacts do not enforce hard force/friction constraints.
claims: Coupled body/contact refinement is distinct from merely adding a contact label
Learned grounding is not a support-force certificate

title: GraCE: Gravity-Guided Contact Dynamics Estimation from 3D Human Motions
author: Cuong Le, Urs Waldmann, Bastian Wandt, Marten Wadenback
snippet: Preprint combines height, velocity and CoG-relative priors with motion-derived forces; force cancellation and deliberate static exertion remain ambiguous.
claims: Height/velocity are insufficient for actual load distribution
Latest force predictors still rely on assumptions and motion precision

title: Human motion capture, reconstruction, and musculoskeletal analysis in real time
author: Urbano Lugris, Manuel Perez-Soto, Florian Michaud, Javier Cuadrado
snippet: Multiple external contacts make inverse-dynamics reaction allocation indeterminate without additional measured forces or assumptions.
claims: Exact multi-contact load is not uniquely recovered from kinematics alone

title: PhysCap: Physically Plausible Monocular 3D Motion Capture in Real Time
author: Soshi Shimada et al.
snippet: Learned foot contacts and constrained physics optimizer use ground reaction plus residual root forces.
claims: Candidate contact and physical optimization are separate stages

title: PhysCap demo release, pinned code
author: Soshi Shimada et al.
snippet: stage3 and util_opt implement foot/toe/heel force QPs; this is not a general whole-body contact discovery implementation.
claims: A compact floating-base force feasibility solve has inspectable code
No tested drop-in CozyClay support

title: PPR diffphys, pinned code
author: Gengshan Yang et al.
snippet: Warp/PyTorch articulated imitation; default data path is quadruped and inspected contact kernel is ground-plane penalty dynamics.
claims: Physical model/input adaptation is required; human template alone is not compatibility evidence

title: PhysPT, pinned code
author: Yufei Zhang, Jeffrey O. Kephart, Zijun Cui, Qiang Ji
snippet: Pretrained SMPL motion/force prediction with selected ground contact vertices and separately predicted root residual; not arbitrary object support discovery.
claims: A force predictor prior does not certify target-avatar support
